decisive_items: compound heterozygous sequence variation in GGCX gene
Low clotting activity of factor X (52.2%; reference range, 77%-131%)
excessive calcification of elastic fiber fragments scattered in the reticular dermis (von Kossa staining)
response.rationale: GGCX deficiency uniquely explains both the PXE-like calcific elastic fiber skin changes and the low factor X/prolonged PT, while pseudoxanthoma elasticum accounts for skin/histology but not the coagulation defect, and cutis laxa only explains skin laxity.

rejected.why: Matches the skin findings and elastic fiber calcification but does not explain low factor X activity or prolonged prothrombin time.
Explains progressive skin laxity and sagging but not yellowish papules, elastic fiber calcification, or the coagulation abnormality.
